messages.subject: RE: [r-inla] Can the variables in INLA-SPDE can be categorical?
parts:
As I understand these questions:

 

  1. Yes
  2. Yes, in the sense that you can have non-spatial covariates generally; technically the spde covariates tend to take continuous inputs but sometimes they can be binned along their continuums for smoothing purposes;
  3. I have not had this be a problem.  If multicollinearity is a concern with fixed effects, you can certainly adjust the priors and/or use ridge regression to force the predictive parameter space to make sharper decisions about how the coefficients are allocated. For latent effects (random effects, etc.) collinearity is rarely a serious concern.  If necessary to tease out additional effects, you can use nesting or varying slopes. Nesting is less computationally expensive and often works just as well if not better.

 

Jonathan

 

Sent from Mail for Windows 10

 

From: Jian WANG
Sent: Tuesday, April 28, 2020 8:34 AM
To: R-inla discussion group
Subject: [r-inla] Can the variables in INLA-SPDE can be categorical?

 

Hi there,

 

I have three questions about the INLA-SPDE model:

(1) Can the response variable be a binary variable?

(2) Can the covariates be categorical variables?

(3) If multicollinearity exists among the covariates, whether the response variable obtained will be unreliable?

 

Thank you.

 

Jian
